rounding_convention: decimal.Decimal throughout; each computed period figure quantized to cents with ROUND_HALF_UP (per-period rounding). Bonds purchased at par, so there is no premium/discount schedule; all amounts land on whole dollars and journal entries are stated in whole dollars. Accrued interest uses the 30/360-style months convention (months/12) implied by the Jul 1 dating and Jun 30/Dec 31 coupon dates.

notes: Purchase at par => investment carried at amortized cost 60,000 with no amortization; the 1,800 of interest accrued Jul 1 -> Nov 1 is paid to the seller and debited to Interest Receivable (some texts debit Interest Revenue instead and then record only the net 900 credit on Dec 31 -- Year 1 net interest revenue of 900 is identical either way). Under the LO 14-7 period-end-only FVA policy the Debt Investments account always shows amortized cost and the separate Fair Value Adjustment valuation account carries the cumulative unrealized amount, so (i) 12/31/Y1 needs a 3,000 credit FVA and a 3,000 unrealized loss in income, (ii) the 3/15/Y2 sale is measured against amortized cost 60,000 giving a 2,400 REALIZED loss (not the 600 gain you would get against the 57,000 fair-value carrying amount) and FVA is deliberately left alone, and (iii) 12/31/Y2 removes the now-orphaned 3,000 FVA credit with a 3,000 unrealized holding GAIN. Year 2 net gain/(loss) effect is therefore +600, and 3,000 loss in Y1 plus 600 gain in Y2 nets to the true 2,400 economic loss. March 1/1 -> 3/15 accrued interest is ignored per the stem's clean-price instruction, so no interest revenue or receivable is recorded in Year 2.
